children: Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices rose to their highest intraday levels since late 2022 on Monday, as diplomatic efforts to open the Strait of Hormuz faltered at a time when Europe is heading into winter with decades-low storage.

The benchmark Dutch front-month contract at the TTF hub (TFMBMc1) was €4.45 higher at €83.97 per megawatt hour (MWh) by 0815 GMT, ICE data showed. It hit an intraday high of €84.50 earlier in the session, which is the highest level since December 22, 2022.
The British front-month contract (NGLNMc1) rose by 10.64 pence to 208.90 pence per therm, the highest since December 23, 2022, ICE data showed.

Iranian officials had said they would attend a gathering with Gulf Arab states to present an agreement with Oman on governing shipping routes through the strait, through which about a fifth of global oil and LNG supplies transited before the war.

Hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough in the near term faded, however, when Oman's Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi posted late on Sunday that the meeting scheduled for Monday had been postponed "in the interests of consensus".

"The market is dominated by escalating Middle East risks, and amid a period of heavy maintenance in Europe affecting Norwegian supply and LNG sendout, bullish price momentum is likely to persist throughout the week," said LSEG analyst Dzmitry Dauhalevich.

Global LNG supply could decline by more than 20 billion cubic meters this winter if Hormuz remains closed, while piped gas has limited upside flexibility, said Gergely Molnar, gas analyst at the Paris-based International Energy Agency.

EU storage levels are standing 20%, or almost 17 bcm, below their five-year average and are trending to their lowest fill levels since 2013. This more limited safety buffer could heat up competition for flexible LNG, fuelling winter price volatility, he added.
Last week, the Netherlands lowered its winter gas storage target to 64% to reduce pressure on suppliers and ease prices.
In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract
was up €1.61 at €87.13 per metric ton.
